newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy urges roundtable talks in Serbia.
newsitem.headline: Italy urges roundtable talks in Serbia.

text.p: Italy, welcoming the OSCE's call for Belgrade to respect opposition victories in local elections, said on Friday that Serbia's government and opposition should now meet to draw up plans for democratic change.
"The Italian government believes there is no alternative to serious and constructive dialogue," the Foreign Ministry said in a statement.

"The current impasse...can only be overcome with a political solution, including a roundtable...to define the terms of a peaceful transition to democracy, which would also pave the way for electoral reform ahead of political polls in 1997."

An OSCE mission to Belgrade headed by former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez urged Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic to install "real democracy" and to restore opposition election victories annulled by the courts.
Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini issued a seperate statement calling on Belgrade "to respect the OSCE's recommendations, expecially regarding the towns where the vote results were annulled."
